▶ Watch the source method (12 min)

Market status: Uptrend Under Pressure — the MSI daily scan flags new buys not recommended. This strategy is a pullback-in-uptrend method; a weak tape removes the big winners while leaving the loss rate intact. Treat this page as names to watch.

The method

From the source video's own closing slide. Where anything else conflicts, this wins.

1 · Look for strength in a consolidation

  • Higher lows through the base
  • EMA and AVWAP reclamation
  • Rising EMAs with price surfing on them
  • Narrowing range

2 · Look for an intraday flush on multiple support points

AVWAP + EMAs, or AVWAP + horizontal supports, or more such combinations. The stack is deliberately open-ended — across the seven worked examples in the video the composition differs every time, and two of them involve no AVWAP+EMA pairing at all (one is AVWAP + a horizontal floor, one is an unfilled gap + the 9-EMA).

3 · Buy the flush

  • When the stock turns positive on the day, OR when the close is above the support levels
  • Prefer entry points with super-tight stop losses
What a "flush" is. Price breaks below the support stack intraday and is rejected from underneath — a failed breakdown. The bar shows a long lower wick and closes back above the level. It is not a rejection at AVWAP from above; that is AVWAP acting as resistance, which is the bearish case.

Entry, stop and exit

ElementRuleWhy
EntryOn the flush bar: when the stock turns positive on the day (i.e. back above the prior close), or on a close above the stack Both are used in the source; they are different prices on the same bar
Stop lossThe low of the flush day Typically 1–4%. The tight stop is the entire edge
ExitClose below the 9-EMA (fast movers) or the 21-EMA (slower ones)21-EMA trails looser and keeps you in longer
PositionSize from the stop distance A 1% stop and a 5% stop are not the same trade
Expectancy warning — stated by the source itself. These tight-stop pullback buys "fail a lot more than they work". The trader is wrong roughly 85% of the time; the system works because the average win is about 7× the average loss. The 20–31× examples in the video are the survivors, selected after the fact — not the expectancy. Our own mechanical replay of seven hand-picked winners reproduced the entries accurately but produced mostly losses, which is exactly what an 85% loss rate predicts.

How these stocks were selected

Two stages. The first is a cheap CSV screen over the whole MarketSmith universe; the second fetches price history only for the survivors.

All NSE stocks 5,817→RS_Rating >= 70 1,747→MCap >= Rs 1000 Cr 708→Turnover >= Rs 5 Cr/day 599→2-30% off the 52W high 528→above the 200-DMA 511→Base = Forming 119→Base stage ['1', '2'] + variants 101→Industry group rank <= 60 42→A/D in ['A', 'B'] 41
Two notes on the screen.
  • The RS gate uses RS_3_Month/RS_6_Month, which are 1–99 percentile ratings, not percent moves. The real "+30% in 1/3/6 months" momentum rule is applied afterwards from actual price history.
  • The A/D gate is currently non-binding — it cut 29 → 29. Everything surviving the RS and group-rank gates already carried A or B. It is in place, but it did not shape this list.

Reading the states. FLUSH + RECLAIM pierced the stack and closed back above it — the trigger. FAILED RECLAIM pierced it and closed below — the level broke, no trade. AT ZONE sitting on the stack, no flush yet. APPROACHING still above the stack — no pullback to support yet.

AVWAP support vs overhead is the polarity flip the video leans on: the AVWAP anchored at the pivot acts as resistance until it is reclaimed, then as support. A name flushing its EMAs while still below its AVWAP has unsold supply overhead — the weaker version of the setup.
